newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mostly higher as stocks weaken.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mostly higher as stocks weaken.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mostly higher after a choppy session, helped late by a weakening stock market.
Standard and Poor's 500 futures showed the most weakness in the stock indexes, sliding more than eight points in afternoon trading.
"In the IMM that's all we were focused on was the stock trade," said Mike Malpede, senior currency analyst with Refco. "The markets are really looking for direction," he said.
March yen closed in the top quarter of its range after a late flurry of buying and strength all session.
After stumbling to a contract low on Friday and again overnight, yen recovered most of Friday's losses on overnight comments from a Japanese official that sparked fears of Japanese intervention.
Japanese Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa said Japan would act appropriately to deal with "excessive" movements in the currency markets.
March yen set a session high early in the day at $0.008747, just short of Friday's high at $0.008751.
Traders said an underlying bullish dollar sentiment kept yen gains in check.
Sterling finished higher after enduring a volatile IMM session, with stop-loss activity noted on both sides of the market, traders said.
Analysts said sterling continues to be well supported, yet capped by resistance above 1.70.
Refco's Malpede said volatility in the contract on Monday stemmed from confusion over the British interest rate outlook.
One IMM trader said the pit was not liquid enough to absorb stop-loss orders in sterling, exacerbating the moves.
"Dealers and locals were really pushing it around," he said.
"I think there's just a lot of volatility at this level since they want to pop up to $1.70 again," another IMM trader said.
She added that yen's moves were confined to a range set early in the day.
"Yen seemed a little quiet today," she said. "All the news came out of Tokyo overnight and so most of that move was early."
She said the currency markets were slowly getting back to normal staffing levels after year-end seasonal holidays, and traders were gearing up for the next U.S. employment report.

At settlement, March yen was up $0.000052 to $0.008731, marks ended up $0.0005 to $0.6425, Swiss francs rose $0.0024 to $0.7440, sterling rose $0.0048 to $1.6910, Canadian dollar rose $0.0029 to $0.7357, Australian dollar fell $0.0021 to $0.7881, and Mexican peso rose $0.000200 to $0.122625.
